features: 5 real features vs all 12, full data vs exp004's complete-case subset
notes: isolate exp004's 3.6pt gap into population-selection vs missing-interaction-terms vs value of the 7 weak features
conclusion: KEEP, major finding. On full 691k rows: LGBM(5 real feat)=0.94351 vs LGBM(12 feat, exp001)=0.96384 -> the 7 'weak' features add +0.0203 jointly despite ~noise-floor univariate AUC individually. On identical complete-case subset (apples-to-apples): logistic linear=0.92735 -> +squares=0.93990 -> +pairwise=0.94477 -> LGBM(5feat)=0.95439 -> LGBM(12feat)=0.96983. Pairwise interaction terms recovered most (not all) of the linear-vs-LGBM gap on the SAME 5 features, confirming real interaction structure beyond sigmoid(linear). Separately, LGBM(5feat) full-data (0.94351) vs subset (0.95439) shows complete-case rows are ~1.1pt 'easier' -- a real but modest population effect. BIGGEST TAKEAWAY: the 7 'weak/noise' features (sleep_hours, notifications_per_day, app_opens_per_day, age, gender, stress_level, academic_work_impact) collectively add ~1.5-2.0 AUC points via joint/interaction signal invisible to univariate analysis -- do NOT drop them based on univariate AUC alone. Revises earlier premature 'gender looks droppable' framing. exp006 queued to decompose which subgroup (weak-numeric vs weak-categorical) drives this and to directly CV-ablate gender alone.

notes: decompose exp005's +0.0154 joint-signal gain by feature subgroup; directly CV-ablate gender
conclusion: KEEP, resolves the question. Gain is 100% from the 4 weak NUMERIC features (+0.01548: sleep_hours, notifications_per_day, app_opens_per_day, age) despite their near-noise univariate AUC -- they carry real joint/interaction signal. The 3 categoricals (gender, stress_level, academic_work_impact) contribute -0.00002, i.e. zero within noise. Dropping gender alone from the full model costs -0.00003 (noise-floor, fold std ~0.0005). DECISION: finalize feature set as the 9 numeric features only, drop all 3 categoricals -- confirms the user's original visual read on the Gender chart, now backed by CV ablation rather than univariate stats. Lesson for teaching: weak univariate AUC does not imply a feature is safe to drop in a tree ensemble -- must CV-ablate, since some weak-looking numerics (sleep_hours/age/etc.) turned out to carry real conditional signal while equally-weak-looking categoricals did not.

features: 9 numeric + 10 pairwise products of the 5 real features (19 total)
preprocessing: products computed on raw values, NaN-propagating, no imputation
notes: Phase 4 first targeted FE attempt, guided by exp009 SHAP interactions
conclusion: REJECT for tree models. -0.00033 vs exp008 (within fold-std noise, not a real regression, but definitely not an improvement either). Interpretation: XGBoost can already approximate these 2-way products via 2 sequential splits on the raw features it has, so explicit product columns are redundant information that only dilutes colsample_bytree's feature sampling (now 19 candidates instead of 9) without adding anything the tree couldn't already build. LESSON: SHAP interaction values tell you what the model is USING, not what it's MISSING -- explicit interaction terms mainly help models that structurally cannot form products on their own (linear/logistic/NN), not tree ensembles with enough depth/estimators. Keep these 10 pairwise-product columns in reserve for the logistic-regression / NN branch of a future ensemble stack instead of the tree pipeline.

conclusion: KEY FINDING. Error (squared, Brier-style) rises 2.5x as missing count in the 5 real features goes 0->5 (0.061->0.150, corr=0.075 -- real but modest). BIGGER pattern: error is concentrated in daily_screen_time_hours 0.5-7h range (err ~0.10-0.13) and collapses near-zero above ~9h where the label is essentially deterministic (matches exp002's sigmoid saturation) -- this is where the OTHER features must resolve ambiguity, so missingness there hurts most. Error-vs-predicted-probability shows the expected symmetric Bayes-error bump near p=0.5 -- model is well-calibrated, not systematically biased. CONCLUSION: imputation is evidence-backed (not a guess) but the modest missingness-error correlation means it likely yields a modest gain, not the whole 0.0066 gap -- test cheaply (median imputation) before escalating to model-based imputation. exp015 queued.

preprocessing: per-fold median imputation (fit on train fold only)
notes: cheapest imputation test, motivated by exp014 error analysis
conclusion: REJECT, do not escalate to model-based imputation. -0.00027 vs exp008 native NaN handling (0.96461), within noise floor but wrong direction. Matches known ML behavior: unconditional median imputation destroys information XGBoost's native missing-direction learning already exploits (it picks an empirically optimal split direction per node, vs one fixed substitute value that can be actively misleading for rows where the true value differs a lot from the median). LESSON per Phase 13 compute efficiency: the cheap test going the WRONG direction is itself informative -- don't escalate to expensive model-based imputation (IterativeImputer/MICE) chasing this lever further, expected value dropped. PIVOT: 4 experiments in a row (exp010 FE, exp011/012 HPO, exp015 imputation) have failed to beat exp008/exp013 by tinkering within the same boosted-tree-on-9-features setup. exp013 diagnosed WHY ensembling stalled (0.99+ OOF correlation among tree models) -- next move is a structurally different model (regularized linear/logistic using the exp010 pairwise-product features, which trees don't need but a linear model does) to actually decorrelate the ensemble, not another tree variant.

notes: diversity model for ensemble; corr with tree ensemble=0.88404; blend AUC=0.96476
conclusion: REJECT for the blend, but diagnostically important. Achieved real decorrelation (corr 0.884 vs tree-vs-tree 0.993-0.995) confirming the diversity hypothesis was directionally right, but individual AUC (0.92451) is 4pts below the tree ensemble -- too large a skill gap for a linear weighted blend to extract value from; optimizer correctly assigned it 0 weight, blend AUC unchanged at 0.96476. Notably WORSE than exp004's similar complete-case-only logistic (0.94477) despite more data/features here -- likely because per-fold median imputation of the ~43% of rows missing at least one of the 5 real features distorts a LINEAR model's fit directly (imputed value enters the dot product as if real), whereas exp004 simply excluded those rows. LESSON: diversity is necessary but not sufficient for ensemble gain -- a weak-but-diverse model still needs to clear a minimum accuracy bar (or use stacking instead of linear blending) to matter. PIVOT: try a small MLP next -- can learn interactions itself (no hand-crafted terms/imputation-sensitivity issue the same way) and has a realistic shot at closing enough of the accuracy gap for its architectural diversity to actually pay off in the blend.

column15: MAJOR CHECKPOINT. Public LB = 0.96606 vs our CV OOF = 0.96476 -- delta +0.00130, larger than fold-noise floor (~0.0005), a real and HEALTHY-direction signal: full-data model (691k rows) beats the CV estimate (avg of 5 folds each trained on ~80%/553k rows), exactly as expected since more data helps a still-data-hungry GBM ensemble generalize better. CV remains trustworthy for RANKING experiments against each other (that's all we used it for); going forward expect real LB to land ~0.0013 above whatever CV says. TRUE gap to public #1 is now 0.97134-0.96606=0.00528 (smaller than the 0.0066 CV implied). Also: no evidence the train/test distribution shift (Phase 0 adversarial AUC=0.565) is hurting us -- if it were, LB would likely have come in BELOW CV, not above. DECISION: trust the CV-driven experiment log's relative conclusions; use this LB checkpoint as the reference point for evaluating all future submissions.

conclusion: REJECT hypothesis, marginal KEEP for ensemble diversity only. Now genuinely converges (best_iter 5720-7336, well under the new 12000 cap, confirming real convergence unlike exp007's 4979-4998/5000). Only +0.00023 over exp007 (noise floor) and still -0.00091 below XGBoost. CONCLUSION: undertraining was NOT the reason CatBoost trailed -- it converges to essentially the same place either way. CatBoost's default depth=8 symmetric-tree architecture genuinely fits this data slightly worse than XGBoost's config; closing that gap would need CatBoost-specific HPO (untested), not more iterations. Use this version (slightly better, and now legitimately converged) in place of exp007 for any future ensemble work. PIVOT: single-lever nudges to the existing tree pipeline are exhausted (exp010 FE, exp011/012 HPO, exp015 imputation, exp019 iterations all failed to move the needle; exp013 tree-ensembling and exp016/017 diversity-model-blending both hit real limits). The one Phase 8 lever not yet tried is proper STACKING (nonlinear meta-learner on OOF predictions) rather than simple linear blending -- a stacker could exploit the logistic/MLP models' real decorrelation (0.884/0.920 corr) in ways a single global blend weight cannot, e.g. trusting them more in specific regions of feature space.

features: 5 base OOF preds as meta-features (lgbm/catboost-v2/xgboost/logistic/mlp), plus 3-tree-only control
cv_strategy: second-level StratifiedKFold n=5 seed=42 on top of already-OOF base predictions
notes: Phase 8: does a real meta-learner beat exp013's simple weighted blend?
conclusion: REJECT all 4 variants. Best result (tree3+Logistic=0.96476) just reproduces exp013's direct-AUC-optimized weights -- no improvement. Adding the 2 diverse-but-weak models (logistic, mlp) to a linear meta-learner made things WORSE (0.96436) -- likely overfitting noisy coefficients on 5 collinear-ish features. Nonlinear GBM meta underperformed the simple blend even as a 3-tree-only control (0.96467 vs 0.96476), suggesting the extra model complexity just adds variance here, not signal. CONCLUSION: with only 3-5 meta-features and a 4pt accuracy gap on the diversity models, there's no room for a meta-learner to find location-dependent trust rules beyond what a single global weight already captures. Ensembling/stacking this feature/model set is now genuinely exhausted -- 8 experiments (exp010,011/012,015,016,017,019,020) have all failed to beat exp013's 0.96476 CV / the resulting 0.96606 LB. Remaining untried, genuinely different levers: (a) much larger/better-resourced HPO across all 3 tree models (only one undersized attempt so far), (b) multi-seed bagging of the final full-data models for a cheap, low-risk, reliable small LB gain (variance reduction, not a modeling improvement) -- doing this next as a safe capstone rather than another speculative single-lever experiment.
